title: What is the best workflow for aigamedev? Three.js or Godot? Or something else?
author: Own_Mix_2744

comments.author: -Unpaid_Wizard-
comments.body: This question is far too broad to be accurately answered

comments.author: weverz
comments.body: Well that's a big big difference

replies.author: weverz
replies.body: Threejs is a for web, a JavaScript library for 3d stuff. Godot is a game engine.

replies.author: Delyzr
replies.body: Godot can also export to wasm for browsergames

replies.author: weverz
replies.body: Yeah but you don't need anything MCP related when using threejs

comments.author: JjyKs
comments.body:
If you know what you're doing and can architect and plan the project good, I gotta say lightweight custom engine built just for your games needs with self documenting system.

I've had way less problems with AI rewriting stuff that already exists when it doesn't have any memories about the engines past versions and the engines codebase stays small enough that the agent can actually check how something works.

replies.author: Own_Mix_2744
replies.body: yeah, so basically use three.js or other framework like phaser.js, and build a little game engine on top of it, right?

replies.author: JjyKs
replies.body:
Well if you want to use web technologies. I used C++ and built a cross platform Vulkan/Metal rendering system but that’s what we use at work so I’m familiar with it. 

Can’t say how it handles web frameworks. My usual feeling is that since I’m not that familiar with those, Claude will create pretty suboptimal project hierarchy and I have no idea how to guide it to do better.
